    As of mid-April 2026, the total U.S. national debt has surpassed
    trillion. This figure, tracking toward 100% or more of the nation’s annual GDP, represents an accumulation of budget deficits funded by Treasury securities. Interest costs are rising significantly, with annual interest payments on this debt exceeding
    billion. 
    Key details about the U.S. national debt include: 
    • Total Debt Level: The gross national debt reached approximately
      trillion as of February 2026, with daily updates often pushing it toward the
      trillion mark.
    • Components of Debt: The debt consists of over
      trillion held by the public (including foreign investors, the Federal Reserve, and private entities) and over
      trillion in intragovernmental holdings (debt owed to government accounts like Social Security)
      .
    • Interest Payments: Interest costs are a rapidly growing budgetary expense, with reports indicating they could exceed national defense spending by 2029.
    • Rising Burden: The debt-to-GDP ratio has reached high levels, indicating that the debt is growing faster than the economy produces goods and services. 
    The debt rises when the federal government runs a budget deficit, spending more on programs, services, and interest than it collects in revenue, such as taxes.
